title: Deep Future VC invests in EvoChip
author: Pablos Holman
authorTitle: Co-Founder and Managing Partner at Deep Future VC
excerpt: Pablos Holman's Deep Future leads seed round to accelerate logic-first synthesis development for global AI infrastructure.
content:
###From Alain Blancquart, EvoChip CEO:
I am pleased to confirm the investment of Deep Future VC in EvoChip. This is really for the AI semiconductor and software market a strong signal that our patented technology provides a unique differentiator: Up to 1000 time more computing power with a 1000 times less energy consumption.

###From Pablos Holman Co-Founder and Managing Partner at Deep Future VC:
Computers got twice as fast on a schedule every two years like clockwork for my entire lifetime. Along the way, we marveled at the self-fulfilling prophecy of Moore's Law, which might as well have been tattooed onto the frontal lobe of every forehead in Silicon Valley. We'd been deceived by cause and effect. Moore's law was Intel's product roadmap. This squelched any other innovation in computation because if competing with an exponential growth doesn't scare off investors, competing with a "law" will.

Finally in the last decade, it became irrefutable that transistor density would not continue to keep doubling. Intel's marketing department is still acting like a cartoon coyote that ran off a cliff and is trying to ignore gravity. Sorry Intel, but the laws of physics are actual laws.

For decades, one of the only successful deviations from Intel's worldview was the advent of the graphics co-processor. The GPU. A dramatically more efficient way to process the kind of data needed for graphics, these chips found their way into all of our computers starting with video games and evolving into the preferred way to compute AI models.

What should have happened, is that a multitude of new approaches to improving computing should have been invented and developed. With no practical route to market, we lived through long, cold, silent winter with almost no innovation in computation. That winter is over. Every day, I see new algorithms, new chip architectures, new ways of making computers faster. A hundred times faster, a thousand times faster, sometimes a million times faster.

The seeming glut of computation was largely used to create layers of abstraction. This made it easier to design computers and create software for them. You'd hardly notice, it just takes more memory, more computation. For example, the number 2 in Python consumes 28 bytes of memory. That's 224 bits, doing a job that could have been done with two. Performing a computation like 2+2 in Python will typically use millions of transistors on a CPU, even though it could be done with three dozen. A modern deep learning model experiences this as compounding inefficiencies. Exponential friction.

EvoChip has invented a combination of new mathematical approaches and evolutionary algorithms to rebuild the stack from transistors all the way up to computational models. This new approach allows for increased efficiency by eliminating many calculation cycles and successive layers of processing. Already experiencing over 1000x performance improvements for quantitative AI applications, EvoChip radically changes the balance of power in computation and therefore lowers drastically the energy consumption.

There aren't enough venture firms with competency to invest in chip advancements which has made me reluctant to back most of the things we see. It can be difficult to get a new chip made. EvoChip is uniquely valuable in either software or hardware. They can support customers in software today, and will become a part of future chip designs once the industry catches onto what they can do. If you know people with computationally intensive models that can't get their hands on a zillion H100s, send them to EvoChip. The team is always looking for more high value use cases to prove themselves.

Pablos Holman
deepfuture.tech VC & Podcast

title: AI at the Edge can't wait for better chips
author: Alain Blancquart
excerpt: Why the current 'better silicon' roadmap fails industrial IoT and how logic synthesis bypasses physical scaling limits.
content:
For years, artificial intelligence has advanced by chasing scale: more data, more compute, bigger models. But this approach has reached its limits.

EvoChip's fundamental premise centers on relocating intelligence away from centralized data centers. We target deployment in homes, hospitals, factories, and vehicles — where power is scarce, silicon is constrained, and intelligence must operate at the edge.

###The Problem
Edge devices face genuine constraints. They operate on minimal power budgets, lack adequate cooling systems, and possess limited silicon resources. Traditional AI infrastructure—optimized for GPUs and matrix mathematics—proves incompatible with these environments due to excessive power consumption, memory requirements, and poor scalability under resource constraints.

###The Solution
Rather than optimizing existing approaches, EvoChip developed alternative technology using evolutionary learning algorithms and binary logic structures. This removes dependence on floating-point mathematics, matrix multiplications, and GPUs entirely.

The architecture has achieved up to 1,000x efficiency gains in testing, including processing over 1 billion inferences per second on a 9-volt-powered $200 FPGA board.

Importantly, the architecture maintains scalability across the entire spectrum—from embedded devices through large language model training.

###Reframed Expectations
Rather than accepting edge AI as merely scaled-down central intelligence, we present it as "smarter" rather than "lite" AI. Models demonstrate enhanced robustness, faster adaptation, and improved generalization across unpredictable environments.

###Implementation
The technology is delivered as modular intellectual property, deployable across existing FPGAs, custom ASICs, or hybrid software-hardware systems without requiring complete model redesign.

Distributed, efficient AI architectures represent the future, particularly as intelligence increasingly embeds itself in consumer devices and industrial systems.

title: The efficiency race: Why the future of AI depends on doing more with less
author: Alain Blancquart
excerpt: Inferences per second has become the critical metric in AI development, driven by concerns about energy consumption and computational efficiency.
content:
"Inferences per second" has become the critical metric in AI development, driven by concerns about energy consumption and computational efficiency. While AI capabilities have expanded dramatically—from voice assistants to medical diagnostics—the power requirements remain unsustainable.

###Three Core Concerns
**Sustainability:** Resource-constrained environments (rural clinics, autonomous drones, disaster zones) cannot rely on traditional cloud infrastructure, making local efficiency essential rather than optional.

**Environmental Impact:** A single query to a large model like GPT-4 can consume as much energy as an oven running for a second. With billions of daily queries, this accumulates to gigawatt-hour scale consumption.

**Access:** The competitive frontier has shifted from maximizing model size to optimizing efficiency—democratizing AI access for nonprofits, startups, and developing nations while reducing carbon emissions.

###Practical Solutions
Dual-AI systems where lightweight scout models handle routine tasks can reduce energy consumption over 85% while maintaining accuracy. Model compression techniques like pruning and quantization present viable approaches.

###The Path Forward
The path forward requires:
- Designing efficiency-focused chips
- Optimizing models for speed and energy
- Implementing new benchmarking standards like "inferences per watt"
- Transparency mechanisms similar to nutrition labels for software

AI advancement is fundamentally about teaching models to think like engineers—and do more with less.

title: EvoChip.ai launches revolutionary AltiCoreAI
author: Alain Blancquart
excerpt: Official reveal of the AltiCoreAI product ecosystem, spanning MCU firmware to synthesizable silicon blueprints.
content:
EvoChip.ai has introduced AltiCoreAI, an advanced IP-based technology designed to transform artificial intelligence inference capabilities.

###Performance
The solution achieves over 3 billion inferences per second on entry-level hardware like the Xilinx ZCU104 when processing datasets such as MNIST—substantially outperforming conventional solutions that typically manage under 10 million IPS on comparable systems.

The technology operates efficiently with minimal data requirements, enabling accurate predictions from significantly smaller datasets than traditional AI models demand.

###Delivery Model
Rather than functioning as conventional software, AltiCoreAI comes as a customizable IP block for integration into applications, SoCs, FPGAs, and custom silicon designs.

**Supported Platforms Include:**
- Windows and Linux environments
- CUDA-enabled GPU systems
- AWS Cloud infrastructure

###Applications
The technology dramatically cuts inference, hardware and energy costs, positioning it for diverse industries including:
- Edge computing
- Autonomous vehicles
- Healthcare diagnostics
- Financial fraud detection
- Predictive maintenance

Early partner integration has commenced, with general availability anticipated later in 2025. The company holds patents pending on this technology.

title: Green AI: EvoChip leads the way towards sustainable technology
author: Alain Blancquart
excerpt: Addressing the environmental cost of matrix-math and the path to zero-emission intelligence.
content:
###The Imperative for Green AI
Artificial intelligence's expansion has driven remarkable progress across numerous sectors, yet it simultaneously demands enormous computational resources. Training sophisticated AI models consumes substantial electrical power, producing significant environmental consequences.

Training a single AI model can produce as much carbon dioxide as five cars over their entire lifetime. This environmental burden demonstrates the urgency for sustainable approaches to AI advancement.

The concept of Green AI acknowledges that environmental concerns transcend purely technical dimensions—they carry ethical implications. As artificial intelligence becomes woven throughout society, addressing the complete supply chain matters: from mineral extraction through semiconductor manufacturing to data center expansion.

###Core Principles of Green AI
The framework emphasizes multiple foundational pillars:
- Energy efficiency
- Carbon footprint reduction
- Ethical considerations
- Life cycle assessment
- Cost reduction
- Universal accessibility

###EvoChip's Innovation Approach
EvoChip's philosophy centers on a straightforward objective: reduce the number of transistors used to train and use the same AI models.

This translates to:
- Diminished rare earth extraction
- Smaller data center requirements
- Reduced energy consumption—potentially by factors exceeding one thousand rather than incremental percentages

The company's proprietary technology demonstrates substantially superior performance compared to conventional neural networks. Researchers approached development without conventional assumptions, creating novel algorithms and advancing mathematical frameworks.

###Conclusion
Green AI signifies an essential transition toward environmentally responsible artificial intelligence development. By emphasizing efficiency, minimizing emissions, and embedding ethical reasoning into technological creation, this approach benefits environmental systems, commercial enterprises, and broader society.

title: Jerry Conrad joins the Board of Directors of EvoChip
author: Alain Blancquart
excerpt: Strategic finance expert Jerry Conrad joins EvoChip to lead M&A positioning and Series A strategy.
content:
Gerald Conrad (Jerry) brings over three decades of financial services expertise to EvoChip's board. His career demonstrates a consistent pattern of leveraging advanced technology and analytics to create a competitive advantage.

###Career Highlights
Conrad's professional accomplishments include founding First National Bank of Marin, the inaugural secured credit card issuer, and Quantitative Data Systems, a processing platform later acquired by Allstate Insurance for its underwriting and fraud detection capabilities.

In 2005, recognizing opportunities in prepaid financial products, Conrad established Primary Innovations, LLC, partnering with MetaBank and MasterCard. His technology platform enabled financial institutions to extend small lines of credit to underbanked populations through prepaid debit cards.

The resulting iAdvance program won "Best New Product" at the 2008 Prepaid Cards Expo, processing millions of transactions and supporting over $500 million in annual funding before the company's 2009 sale to Cash America.

###Current Roles
Currently, Conrad serves as Chairman of Memo Financial Services, Inc., a major money services business established in 1986. Memo operates across 26 states through 3,200 agents, delivering money orders, bill payment services, and prepaid card solutions to millions annually.

Beyond EvoChip, Conrad holds board positions with Liquid Biosciences and Pave Finance Inc., maintaining involvement across biotech, fintech, and emerging technology sectors.

title: Can AI avoid hitting the wall?
author: Alain Blancquart
excerpt: An analysis of thermodynamic limits in neural network scaling and the necessity of deterministic logic.
content:
AI represents the fastest-growing technological demand in history, surpassing both cloud computing and personal computer adoption rates. The technology now pervades finance, healthcare, industry, and social sectors.

###The Cost Problem
However, this expansion comes with escalating costs. Training individual ChatGPT models reportedly exceeds $100 million, creating prohibitive expenses for individuals, SMEs, and large enterprises alike.

Current solutions rely on expanding data center infrastructure with additional servers, but even when considering initiatives consisting of improving today's technology efficiency by X percent (under 100% in the best case), AI will not make it.

###Sustainability Concerns
Sustainability concerns extend beyond economics:
- Projected AI electricity consumption could match Japan's usage by 2027-2030
- Increased water demands for server cooling
- Rare earth extraction for chip manufacturing

###EvoChip's Approach
EvoChip's approach aims to accelerate AI model computation 1,000 times faster within chip architecture, reducing necessary hardware proportionally while maintaining output quality.

The solution employs evolutionary algorithms maintaining linear data relationships rather than exponential complexity, combined with novel mathematical components functioning at the gate level.

###Validation
The company validated its technology with Liquid BioScience, demonstrating significant performance improvements and resource efficiency gains over conventional practices.

title: The inevitable limits of exponential growth in Artificial Intelligence
author: Alain Blancquart
excerpt: Why the 'GPU-for-everything' economic model is about to collapse and what replaces it.
content:
###Introduction
The AI sector has captured global attention for decades with promises of transformative breakthroughs. However, behind the rapid progress lies an often-ignored reality: exponential computational demand will soon collide with limitations in power and cooling infrastructure.

###The Moore's Law Wall
Moore's Law has driven technological progress for decades, but transistors approaching atomic scales encounter physical barriers. The International Data Corporation projects global AI computing capacity demand will increase sixfold by 2025, while total capacity grows only threefold—requiring a 100% efficiency improvement rather than typical single-digit gains.

###Environmental Consequences
Data centers powering AI consume massive electricity quantities. The International Energy Agency estimates data centers will represent approximately 3% of global electricity consumption by 2025.

The New York Times reported GPT-4 consumed between 51,773-62,319 MWh—over 40 times more than GPT-3, equivalent to five to six years of electricity for 1,000 average American households.

###The AI Market Opportunity
McKinsey reports generative AI's annual financial impact at minimum $2.6 trillion, with skyrocketing chip demand. Computing power requirements have doubled every 3.4 months. Gartner projects AI chip revenue will grow from $34 billion in 2021 to $86 billion by 2026.

###What Must Be Done?
Incremental efficiency improvements prove insufficient. The industry needs breakthrough technology delivering at least 1,000-fold hardware requirement reductions—either processing identical results with one server instead of 1,000, or achieving 1,000 times greater results with existing infrastructure.

###EvoChip's Solution
EvoChip technology replaces conventional neural network-based semiconductor stacks with a new approach combining innovative mathematics and evolutionary algorithms. This achieves efficiency ratios approximately 1,000 times better than current methods.

A $300 FPGA card with a 100MHz processor powered by a 9-volt battery can process over one billion data lines per second.

###Case Study: Liquid BioSciences
Liquid BioSciences, a diagnostic biomarker discovery company analyzing 50+ diseases, previously required two to three weeks using 32-server parallel systems, enabling only 10-15 annual studies.

Testing involved colorectal cancer datasets containing 690 patients with nearly 50,000 variables each. Results showed software-only EvoChip operated 3,386 times faster than existing solutions.

EvoChip completed 1,000 runs in 4 minutes 19 seconds versus 14 minutes 37 seconds per single run. Typical projects require approximately 60,000 runs. The colorectal cancer project took 20 days across 30 servers. EvoChip would complete identical work in under 5 hours on single servers.

###Key Features
- Ultra-fast, hyper-efficient, modular, cost-effective AI technology
- Complete technology stack redesign from transistor to application level
- Ultra-low gate count modeling logic
- Massively faster digital logic compared to neural networks
- Minimal energy consumption and heat generation
- No floating-point unit dependency
- Eliminates matrix multiplications
- Massive hardware parallelization capacity
- No custom chip development needed—uses commercial FPGA hardware
- Fastest learning process—over one billion model evaluations per second
